citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration. BlueSky Prototype source and documentation. https://github.com/EIAgov/BlueSky
description: BlueSky Prototype is the U.S. Energy Information Administration's experimental modular energy-system model. Its electricity and hydrogen modules use least-cost linear optimisation, while residential demand responds to prices. An integrator runs modules separately or couples them into a nonlinear problem. Python source, environment instructions, module documentation and a Snakemake crosswalk example are public under Apache-2.0 at no cost. Inputs are module assumptions and example energy/weather relationships; outputs are experimental system solutions and sensitivity calculations. Coverage is deliberately hypothetical: the prototype omits country, region and period labels. EIA states that its results are not applicable to the real world and that further development is paused. The code remains reusable for studying coupling and sensitivity methods in energy-infrastructure simulations. PyPSA (model-pypsa) offers related energy-system optimisation. This resource is distinct from the BlueSky air-traffic simulator. No published energy outlook is represented as a result of this prototype.
name: EIA BlueSky energy-system prototype
